court: Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit

issues.label: Meaning of 'to the extent practicable'
issues.why: The core dispute turns on how § 6(h)(4)'s mandate to reduce exposure 'to the extent practicable' constrains EPA's regulatory choices.

issues.label: Whether cost justifies declining regulation
issues.why: EPA relied on high implementation costs to avoid regulating recycling, requiring the court to decide if cost is a permissible practicability factor.

issues.label: Whether 'low levels' of exposure suffice
issues.why: EPA cited low exposure levels to justify non-regulation, and the court must assess whether that satisfies the statutory reduction mandate.

issues.label: Competing policy goal of promoting recycling
issues.why: EPA invoked its recycling-promotion goal to decline regulation, raising whether such non-TSCA policy considerations are lawful under § 6(h).

issues.label: Reliance on RCRA compliance for disposal
issues.why: EPA justified declining disposal regulation by citing RCRA compliance, and the court must decide if another statute's coverage excuses TSCA action.

issues.label: Adequacy of sewage sludge treatment
issues.why: EPA addressed sludge only 'by reference to a stated factor,' requiring review of whether that response meets § 6(h) obligations.

issues.label: Article exemption for wastewater discharges
issues.why: The water-discharge prohibition excludes articles containing decaBDE, raising whether that carve-out is consistent with the practicability mandate.

issues.label: Validity of staged/phased regulation
issues.why: EPA relies on Bluewater Network to defend regulating incrementally, and the court must determine whether staging is permissible here.

issues.label: Definition of 'article' and its scope
issues.why: The regulatory definition of 'article' shapes what recycling and new-manufacture activities escape regulation.

issues.label: Whether PPE-only recycling rule is adequate
issues.why: EPA required only warning signs and PPE for pallet recycling, raising whether that meaningfully reduces exposure as required.

issues.label: Standard and scope of judicial review
issues.why: The court must identify the applicable TSCA/APA review standard (substantial evidence vs. arbitrary-and-capricious) governing the rule.

issues.label: Adequacy of EPA's explanation/reasoned decisionmaking
issues.why: The court must assess whether EPA adequately justified declining to regulate each of the four contested areas.

issues.label: Whether EPA addressed comments
issues.why: Petitioners submitted comments on all four areas, requiring review of whether EPA meaningfully responded under § 553.

issues.label: Duty to 'address the risks' determined present
issues.why: Section 6(h)(4) requires EPA to address risks it determines are presented, and the court must decide if unregulated exposures were addressed.

issues.label: Justiciability and standing
issues.why: The court must confirm petitioners have standing and the challenges to unregulated areas are justiciable.

issues.label: Timeliness and consolidation of petitions
issues.why: The 2021 and 2024 petitions were consolidated, requiring confirmation both challenges are properly and timely before the court.

issues.label: Status of remanded 2021 Rule
issues.why: The 2021 Rule was voluntarily remanded and held in abeyance, raising whether its challenge remains live or is superseded.

issues.label: Appropriate remedy: remand without vacatur
issues.why: Petitioners seek remand without vacatur plus deadlines, requiring the court to decide the proper remedy and whether it can impose timelines.

issues.label: Authority to impose rulemaking deadlines
issues.why: The court must determine whether it may order EPA to propose and finalize amendments within specified periods.

issues.label: Treatment of protected subpopulations
issues.why: Section 6(h) singles out higher-risk subpopulations, requiring assessment of whether EPA adequately protected them.

issues.label: Deference owed to EPA's statutory interpretation
issues.why: The court must decide how much deference EPA's reading of 'practicable' and § 6(h) receives after Loper Bright.
